items.title: Flatness modulo an ideal plus vanishing of Tor one implies flatness on nilpotently annihilated modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if a module is flat modulo an ideal and Tor one against the quotient by that ideal vanishes, then the module is flat modulo every power and Tor one vanishes against every module annihilated by a power, hence the module is flat when the ideal is nilpotent (statement lines 23867-23879). The proof does not invoke the local criterion: it inducts on the exponent to get flatness modulo each power, and then resolves a module killed by a power through successive quotients, using the long exact Tor sequence (proof lines 23881-23933). Reducing the general module to modules killed by a single power is the step that carries the second part. H2.
